This seems fine for now. FYI I have a PR that solves this by defining the necessary statistics to allow the optimizer to do the join order swap. It’s in draft here: https://github.com/lance-format/lance/pull/7368

I think that will be the better long term solution.

### Relationship to #7368 (TableProvider write inputs / source statistics)

@wjones127 
#7368 also rewrites `create_plan`'s source handling, so the two overlap textually — but they cover different cases and don't conflict semantically:

- **This PR (#7382)** governs **statless stream sources**: it builds `source.join(target)` so the small source is the hash build side and the large target streams as the probe (preventing the per-partition full-target materialization that OOM'd workers). That orientation holds precisely *because* a one-shot stream carries no statistics for `should_swap_join_order` to act on.
- **#7368** keeps stream/spill sources statless (`one_shot_provider` / `spilling_table_provider` report no stats) and only adds exact `num_rows`/`total_byte_size` for **materialized** sources (`MemTable`/file), where the optimizer then picks the build side by cost.

So they partition cleanly: statless stream → explicit source-build (this PR); materialized → stats-driven. The only thing to reconcile is the textual merge in `create_plan` for whichever lands second.

Minor suggestion for #7368: have `test_merge_insert_source_statistics_in_plan` assert the resulting build side (not just that stats reach the plan), so the materialized path's join orientation is pinned alongside this PR's stream-path orientation.

>  so the small source is the hash build side and the large target streams as the probe

FWIW, the source might not always be smaller than the target. In upsert workloads, we only need the `on` columns from the target, but we need all columns from the source. If the `on` is just an integer id, then even on a large table it's not that large.

Agreed the source isn't always smaller by bytes — but for the **streaming** source this PR targets, I think building the source is still the right default regardless of per-row width:

A stream source has to be materialized on a single compute node anyway (it's consumed into one partition's merge, and the hash-join build / index replay buffers it). So it's bounded-by-construction — small enough to fit, or the merge wouldn't run at all. The **target**, by contrast, has no such bound: it's the table, potentially much larger than any one node can hold. Even though the target side projects to just the `on` columns + row ids (narrower per row), it still scales with table size — and that's precisely the side we don't want to collect into the hash build.

So for streams: build the side that must fit in memory anyway (source), stream the unbounded side (target). Width doesn't change which side is bounded.

For materialized sources where the optimizer knows both sizes, #7368's stats-driven swap is the better, general answer — this PR is just the stopgap for the statless stream path.

Gentle ping @wjones127 @Xuanwo — I believe the discussion is resolved: the assertion now checks only the join *orientation* (target on the build side, source streamed on the probe side), not byte size. CI is green. Mind another look when you have a moment?

title: perf: stream the target on the probe side of the merge_insert join
